p:cNvPr.descr: Chains of glycogen synthesis. In the top left is the UDP-glucose chain. It begins with a hexagon in red, with thick lines on the bottom half of the hexagon. Clockwise from the left point around, it is: H binds down to HO (4 in the middle); 6CH2OH binds down to H (inside hexagon and 5 in the middle); O is the third point; H binds down to O (1 in the middle); H (inside hexagon) binds down to HO (2 in the middle); and OH (inside hexagon) binds down to H (3 in the middle). O on the fourth point of the hexagon binds down to (all black) P. P binds left to -O, double binds down to O, and binds right to O, which binds right to P. P double binds up to O, binds right to O-, and down to O, which binds right to CH2. CH2 binds down to H on the 1st point of a pentagon. Clockwise, the second point is O; Uracil binds down to H, H (inside pentagon) binds down to OH on the fourth and fifth points of the pentagon. To the right of this is a blue chain with two exact hexagons. Clockwise: H binds down to HO (4 in middle); CH2OH binds down to H (inside hexagon); O is the third point; H binds down and right to O (1 in middle); H binds down to OH; and OH binds down to H. The O from the fourth point binds right and up to H of the first point of the second hexagon, which is exaclty like the first. Below this blue chain, it states, "Nonreducing end of a glycogen chain with n residues (n > 4)." Below the purple glycogen synthase oval is a line of chains, identified as the new nonreducing end. It begins with a red hexagon. Clockwise: H binds to HO (4 in middle); CH2OH binds down to H (inside hexagon); O is the third point; H binds down and right to O (blue); H (inside hexagon) binds down to OH; and OH (inside hexagon) binds down to H. The blue O binds right and up to H (4 in the middle) for the first point of the next hexagon, all in blue. This is excatly the same as the first red hexagon and is repeated twice. Below this chain, it states, "Elongated glycogen with n + 1 residues.
